svg.aria-label: Diagram: AWS Backup restore testing separates into two claims, only one of which is automatic. The restore testing plan starts a restore job and monitors the time taken to complete the restore, which establishes that a restore job completed and how long it took. Confirming that the restored resource is usable is an optional event-driven validation the customer builds: an EventBridge rule listening for the restore job reaching COMPLETED, a Lambda whose AWS-supplied sample contains only the comment TODO validate the resource, and a call to PutRestoreValidationResult, an API that is not available through the Lambda SDK and needs a Lambda layer. By default the restored data is deleted after the test completes, and retaining it for validation is an opt-in of 1 to 168 hours. The diagram also records three ways a resource leaves a test without failing it: a protected resource with no eligible recovery point is simply not included, a sub-daily cron with a start time later than 11:59 runs only once per day, and tag conditions select the protected resource but are not used to choose which recovery point is restored. Finally it gives the selection window arithmetic: the window is calculated from actual job execution time, so SelectionWindowDays must exceed the backup frequency plus StartWindowHours, which for weekly backups and the 168-hour maximum start window is 14 days.
svg.title: Two claims: a restore job completed, and the restored thing works
svg.text: The plan times the restore. Nothing in it looks at the data.
AWS Backup restore testing — two claims, and only one of them is automatic.
CLAIM 1 — automatic, on your schedule
“starts restore jobs based on your plan and
monitors the time taken to complete the restore”
Establishes: a restore job completed, in N minutes.
Exercises the IAM role, the KMS grants, the subnet
inference — the things that break real restores.
CLAIM 2 — “Optionally”, and you build it
“create a validation workflow with any target
supported by Amazon EventBridge, such as AWS Lambda”
// TODO: Validate the resource
That comment is the whole of AWS’s sample. The API it
reports to is “not available through the Lambda SDK”.
And then the evidence is removed, by default
“By default, this data is deleted after the test is complete.” Keeping it is opt-in: “retain for a specific
number of hours … from 1 to 168 hours”. Right default — and the thing that would answer the question is gone.
Three ways a resource leaves the test without the test failing
1. “If no recovery point for a protected resource is eligible, AWS Backup does not include that protected
resource in the test.” In the plan, not in the run, and the run still passes.
2. “If you create a restore testing plan for “every 12 hours” but provide a start time of later than
11:59, it will only run once per day.” The plan still says every 12 hours.
3. Tags pick the resource, not the backup: “the restored recovery point might not match the tag conditions”.
The arithmetic that keeps recovery points eligible
“The selection window is calculated from the actual job execution time, not the plan’s scheduled start time.”
SelectionWindowDays > backup interval + StartWindowHours weekly + 168h → > 14 days
Write down which claim your last test result supports.
With no validation workflow behind it, the honest sentence is: a restore job completed in N minutes — which
is worth having, and is not: we tested our backups.
Then count: protected resources the plan should cover, against restore jobs the run actually produced.
